notes: The marginal 'Or, oblation' was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
לְפָנֶיךָ divides as rule 30 directs: the preposition and its construct noun share the single 'before', headed on פָּנֶה, while the suffix keeps its own 'thee'.

Competing reading on t018 'the': it could be given to the rectum as the word it stands before, but rule 29's closing paragraph places a chain's single supplied determiner on the construct noun in either English order, and מִנְחָה is the construct here (rule 28 attributive rendering of עָרֶב).
